title: Priority throughput reservations and intelligent drain windows for Dedicated fleets
creator: Sofia Martinez
description: Add an automated maintenance planner and drain orchestration that preserves throughput SLAs for Dedicated fleets. The feature implements: 1) node scoring and window placement that respects model-specific throughput guarantees and customer reserved capacity; 2) pre-drain throughput reservation tokens that gate drains until warm-spare rerouting completes; 3) integration with autoscaler to temporarily hold burst capacity and avoid cascading evictions; and 4) Console hooks for scheduling maintenance windows with visibility into expected token-hours and impact. This ticket covers design, runtime changes to the drain controller, autoscaler policy updates, and Console scheduling UI hooks.
updates: 2025-01-08: RFC created, proposing 'reservation token' primitive for draining nodes to ensure in-flight SLOs are met. Link: https://confluence.redwoodai/internal/dedicated/maintenance-reservation-rfc

2025-01-16: Design review with PM and Runtime team. Decision: reservation tokens are per-fleet and per-model-shape (seq_len + batch distribution). Trade-off: increased allocation complexity vs reduced customer disruption. Action: prototype token allocation in drain-controller.

2025-01-22: Prototype implemented in staging: drain controller holds node in 'reserved' state until warm-spare reroute ACK observed by ingress. Observed 12% reduction in tail-latency spikes during drains in internal perf test (model: llama-70b, seq=2048). Tests: https://github.com/redwood-inference/pilot/pull/512

2025-01-30: Autoscaler policy updated to support 'maintenance_hold' mode that temporarily raises headroom target by configured percent. Simulated scenarios show fewer preemptions but added transient GPU utilization variance. Perf notes and trade-offs recorded in design doc.

2025-02-07: UX spec for Console scheduling added. Includes 'throughput reservation estimate' calc and visualization of token-hours. UX feedback: expose opt-in 'aggressive compacting' option for non-latency-critical customers. Link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1k-Redwood/maintenance-ui

2025-02-12: Integration test failures fixed: edge case when multiple overlapping windows target same AZ. Implemented deterministic node selection by score + stable hash to avoid simultaneous AZ impact. Unit tests added. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/1347

2025-02-15: Preparing canary rollout to 10% of Dedicated fleets. Ops runbook drafted and linked. Next: monitor token exhaustion metrics, KBV of warm-spare latency, and autoscaler oscillation signals. Runbook: https://confluence.redwoodai/internal/ops/maintenance-runbooks
notes: Key implementation points: (1) Reservation tokens are short-lived leases issued by the fleet controller; tokens carry expected throughput units and a routing fingerprint that helps ingress pick a compatible warm spare. (2) Drain controller will signal autoscaler with 'maintenance_hold' which temporarily increases headroom target to accommodate warm-spare buffering. (3) To reduce per-request routing cost, ingress caches mapping of fingerprint -> warm-spare nodes for 30s. Observability: new metrics token_issued, token_expired, token_blocked_drains, maintenance_hold_triggered. Rollout plan includes incremental enablement per-org with an emergency stop via Console.
acceptance_criteria: Console can schedule a maintenance window and show estimated throughput-token-hours
Drain controller issues reservation token and waits for warm-spare ACK before evicting workload
Autoscaler respects maintenance_hold and avoids cascading preemptions in recorded scenarios
Canary rollout on 10% of fleets shows <5% increase in overall cost and <2% customer-facing error rate impact
Instrumentation emitting new metrics and dashboards created in Console for token usage and maintenance impact
